{"command":"cat <<'EOF' > /tmp/create_dist.py
import numpy as np
from scipy.optimize import brentq

N = 150_000
TARGET = 10.0
# One high-probability outcome and N-1 equal low-probability outcomes.
def distribution(x):
    return np.r_[x, np.full(N - 1, (1.0 - x) / (N - 1))]
def kl_values(x):
    p = distribution(x)
    return np.sum(p * np.log(N * p)), -np.mean(np.log(N * p))

# This family has a crossing where forward and reverse KL are both 10.
# Solve their difference first, then refine the shared target by a scalar root.
def difference(x):
    f, b = kl_values(x)
    return f - b

# The low-x side has both divergences large from the many tiny entries;
# the high-x side has forward KL dominant. Find the crossing in logit space.
grid = np.linspace(-30.0, 30.0, 2001)
xs = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-grid))
vals = np.array([difference(x) for x in xs])
interval = next((i for i in range(len(grid)-1) if vals[i] * vals[i+1] <= 0), None)
if interval is None:
    raise RuntimeError('No forward/backward crossing in this family')
x0 = brentq(difference, xs[interval], xs[interval+1], xtol=1e-15)
f, b = kl_values(x0)
p = distribution(x0)
np.save('/app/dist.npy', p)
assert p.shape == (N,) and np.all(p > 0) and abs(p.sum() - 1) < 1e-10
assert abs(f - TARGET) <= 0.001 and abs(b - TARGET) <= 0.001, (f, b)
print(f'Saved /app/dist.npy: sum={p.sum():.16f}, forward={f:.9f}, backward={b:.9f}')
EOF
python /tmp/create_dist.py"}
